Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:10:1.english: It is not the property of the owner of the camel - Rather, [it is the property] of the storekeeper.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:10:2.hebrew: במסכסכת את כל הבירה - שהגמל עובר בפני כל הבירה ומסכסכו, דהא ודאי הוי כולו כמקום גחלת. אבל בעלמא שהאש הולכת מאליה, לאו חציו הן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:10:2.english: Where it ignited the entire building - [Meaning] that the camel passes in front of the entire building and ignites it, for this is certainly all like the place of the coal. However, in general, where the fire goes on its own, it is not [considered] his arrows.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:11:1.hebrew: בשעמדה - עמד הגמל במקומו וסכסך את כל הבירה, שהיתה חבילתו גדולה כנגד כל הבירה. והגמרא לא שבק לאסוקי למילתיה, ופרכיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:11:1.english: Where it stood - The camel stood in its place and ignited the entire building, for its bundle was large, [extending] across the entire building. And the Gemara did not allow [him] to finish his statement, and challenged it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:12:1.english: All the more so - For [the camel's owner] should have hurried and driven it so that it would not ignite [the building].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:12:2.english: When it stood to urinate - For [he] is under unavoidable compulsion, and it ignited [the building].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:1:2.hebrew: סריכא - שנועץ צפרניו בכותל, שאין דרכו בכך, ומשונים הן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:1:2.english: Serikha - That [the goat] digs its claws into the wall, for this is not its normal way, and [thus] they are unusual.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:3:1.english: His fire - [Referring to] one who sets the fire.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:3:2.english: Due to his arrows - Scripture held him liable because he is the one doing [it], for he is like one who shoots an arrow.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:3:3.hebrew: משום ממונו - כשורו ובורו שהזיקו. וקס"ד דאיכא בינייהו כגון שהדליק בגחלת שאינו שלו, דלרבי יוחנן חייב, דחציו הן, ולר"ל פטור, דלאו ממונו הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:3:3.english: Due to his property - Like his ox and his pit that caused damage. And we initially assumed that there is [a practical difference] between them, such as where he lit [a fire] with a coal that is not his: for according to Rabbi Yochanan he is liable, since it is his arrows, whereas according to Reish Lakish he is exempt, since it is not his property.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:4:1.english: This [fire] does not [proceed] from his force - For fire goes and burns afar on its own.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:4:2.hebrew: הא לית ביה ממשא - דשלהבת היא המזקת, דאין לה ממש. הלכך, כי חייביה רחמנא, משום חציו הוא דחייביה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:4:2.english: This [fire] has no substance - For it is the flame that causes the damage, which has no substance. Therefore, when the Merciful One obligated him, it is on account of his arrows that He obligated him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:5:1.hebrew: חציו דכלב הן - דהוה ליה צרורות, הלכך משלם ח"נ. ואדם המדליק, מש"ה חייב נ"ש, שאין דין צרורות באדם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:5:1.english: They are the dog's arrows - For it is [a case of] pebbles; therefore, [the owner] pays half-damages. And [as for] a person who kindles [a fire], that is why he is liable for full damages, because the law of pebbles does not apply to a person.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:6:1.english: [It is] not the property of the owner of the dog - Rather, [it is the property] of the owner of the cake.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:7:1.english: Where it threw it - [Meaning] that it threw it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:7:2.english: He pays half damage - For they are [a case of] pebbles, and the dog caused them. Another version: because it is an unusual [act].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:7:3.hebrew: ועל גדיש כוליה פטור - דאשו משום ממונו, והאי לאו ממונו הוא. וצרורות ליכא למימר, דהא ממקום גחלת ואילך דלקה אש מאליו. ומשום הכי אוקמה בדאדייה אדויי, דאי אנחה עם החררה כי אורחיה, לא מצי למיתני ח"נ אמידי, דאמקום גחלת חייב נזק שלם, דאורחיה הוא ליטול חררה עם הגחלת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:7:3.english: And for the stack as a whole, he is exempt - For one's fire is [liable] because of his property, and this [coal] is not his property. And one cannot say [that he is liable for] pebbles, because from the spot of the coal onward, the fire burned on its own. And for this reason he established [the Mishnah] as dealing with a case where [the dog] threw it, for if it had placed it [there] together with the cake in its normal manner, [the Mishnah] could not have taught "half-damage" regarding anything, since for the spot of the coal he would be liable for full damage, as it is its normal manner to take a cake with the coal.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:7:4.english: And for the place of the coal - the place where the coal fell.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:8:1.hebrew: ור' יוחנן - דאמר אשו משום חציו, מוקים לה בדאנחה כי אורחיה, דעל חררה נ"ש, דשן היא, ואמקום גחלת נ"ש, דאורחיה היא ובידים עבד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:8:1.english: And Rabbi Yochanan - who says [that] one's fire is [liable] because of his arrows, establishes it [the Mishnah] as [referring to a case] where [the dog] placed it down in its usual manner, so that for the cake [he pays] full damage, since it is [a case of] Tooth, and for the place of the coal [he pays] full damage, since it is its usual manner and it did [it] directly.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:8:2.hebrew: ואגדיש כוליה ח"נ - דחציו דכלב הוא, והיינו צרורות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:8:2.english: And for the entire stack [of grain], half damages - For it is the dog's arrows, and that is [the category of] pebbles.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:9:2.hebrew: בנר חנוכה פטור - שמצוה להניחה ברה"ר לפרסומי ניסא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 22a:9:2.english: With a Hanukkah lamp, [he is] exempt - For it is a mitzvah to place it in the public domain to publicize the miracle.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:10:1.english: Where [the camel] ignites the entire building - For all of it is [considered] the place of the coal.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:11:1.hebrew: ואי במסכסכת אמאי חייב - חנווני הכל? גם בעל הגמל יתחייב עמו, כיון שגם הוא פושע בסכסוך. אבל אי בלא מסכסכת ניחא ליה, דלא הוה ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה שיהא נר מבחוץ; אבל כיון דאוקמיה במסכסכת, אי אפשר שלא יראה הדליקה, כיון שדולקת כל כך שמסכסכת כל הבירה דרך הילוכה, והיה לו להרחיק ולמונעה מלהיות הולכת ומסכסכת. אבל אין לפרש "אמאי חייב חנווני" — בעל הגמל יתחייב הכל, דהא לקמן (בבא קמא דף כג.) פריך: "וליחייב בעל הגחלת", ואע"פ שבעל הכלב פשע — גם בעל הגחלת יש לו להתחייב שלא שמר גחלתו. ומשני: כשעמדה — כלומר, לאו במסכסכת דרך הילוכה, אלא בעמדה במקום אחד, והרבה כל כך במשאוי שמסכסכת כל הבירה בעמידה. ופריך: דכ"ש חנווני פטור — לאו פטור לגמרי, אלא כלומר פטור מחלקו של בעל הגמל, דיותר מסכסכת בעמידה משאילו היתה הולכת ועוברת בלי עיכוב. ומשני: כשעמדה להטיל מימיה, דאנוס הוא בעמידה זו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:11:1.english: And if [it is a case] where [the camel] ignited [the building], why is he liable - [Why is] the storekeeper [liable for] everything? The owner of the camel should also be liable with him, since he too was negligent in the igniting. However, if [the case were] without [the camel] igniting [the building], it is understandable, since he [the camel's owner] did not have to consider that there would be a lamp outside; but since he [Reish Lakish] established [the case as one] where [the camel] ignited [the building], it is impossible that he would not see the fire, since it is burning so intensely that it ignites the entire building along its path, and he should have distanced [the camel] and prevented it from going along and igniting [the building]. However, one should not explain "why is the storekeeper liable" [to mean that] the owner of the camel should be liable [for] everything, for later (Bava Kamma 23a) [the Gemara] asks: "And let the owner of the coal be liable!" — [meaning that] even though the owner of the dog was negligent, the owner of the coal should also be liable for not guarding his coal. And [the Gemara] answers: "[The case is] where it stood [still]" — that is to say, not where it ignited [the building] along its path, rather where it stood in one place, and [the owner] loaded so much in the burden that it ignites the entire building while standing. And [the Gemara] asks that all the more so the storekeeper should be exempt — [this does] not [mean] completely exempt, rather it means exempt from the share of the owner of the camel, for it ignites more while standing than if it were walking and passing by without delay. And [the Gemara] answers: "[The case is] where it stood [still] to urinate" — for he is under duress in this standing:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:1:1.hebrew: והתניא הכלב - אמתניתין הו"מ למפרך, אלא נטר עד דמייתי ברייתא ופריך אתרוייהו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:1:1.english: "But isn't it taught [in a baraita]: The dog..." - [The Gemara] could have raised [this] difficulty against our Mishnah, but it waited until it brought the baraita and raised the difficulty against both of them:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:1:2.hebrew: דאפיך מיפך - וא"ת: למ"ד תחילתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס [חייב], לחייב נ"ש, דתחילתו בפשיעה דאורחיה וסופו באונס דלאו אורחיה? וי"ל: דלא אמר משום דתחילתו בפשיעה לגבי רגל לחייב נ"ש לגבי קרן, דאפילו פושע גמור לענין קרן — לא חייבתו תורה אלא חצי נזק. דאי לאו הכי, ארי שנכנס לחצר הניזק וטרף ואכל — לחייב נ"ש, דתחילתו בפשיעה לענין דריסה! וכן כל קרן בחצר הניזק תחילתו בפשיעה לענין שן ורגל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:1:2.english: [Their manners of movement] were changed - And if you ask: according to the one who says [that in a case where] its beginning was with negligence and its end was through unavoidable accident [one is] liable, let him be liable for full damage, since its beginning was with negligence — as it is its normal manner — and its end was through unavoidable accident — as it is not its normal manner? And one can say: he did not say [that] because its beginning was with negligence with respect to Foot, it should make him liable for full damage with respect to Goring; for even [in the case of] one who is completely negligent with respect to Goring, the Torah only obligated him [to pay] half-damage. For if not so, a lion that entered the courtyard of the injured party and tore [an animal] and ate [it] should be liable for full damage, since its beginning was with negligence with respect to treading! And similarly, every [case of] Goring in the courtyard of the injured party has its beginning with negligence with respect to Tooth and Foot:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:1:3.hebrew: גדיא בסריכא - שנועץ צפרניו בארץ וקופץ כמו הכלב, ולא דמי לסרוכי וסליק, שנסרך בחבית עד שמגיע ללפת:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:1:3.english: The goat [moved] by climbing [bisrikha] - [This means] that it digs its claws into the ground and leaps like a dog, and it is not similar to [the case of] "climbing up" [serukhei u'salik], where it climbs along a barrel until it reaches the turnips.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:3:1.hebrew: אשו משום חציו - לא שיבעיר בעצמו האש, אלא כל מקום שפשע ולא שמר גחלתו, חציו נינהו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:3:1.english: His fire is due to his arrows - [This does] not [refer only to a case] where he himself kindles the fire; rather, wherever he was negligent and did not guard his coal, it is [considered] his arrows.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:3:2.hebrew: אשו משום ממונו - כלומר, חיוב ממונו יש בו, ולא שיהא האש שלו; דאפילו הדליק באש של אחר חייב, כדאשכחן בפ' הכונס (לקמן בבא קמא דף נו.) בכופף קמתו של חבירו בפני הדליקה ומטיא ברוח מצויה, וגבי גץ שיצא מתחת הפטיש, אע"ג דמסתמא מפקיר ליה. ועוד, דאין לך אדם שיתחייב בדליקה — שיפקיר הגחלים וידליק גדיש של חבירו! ולא כפ"ה דפי' דאיכא בינייהו דאדליק בגחלת שאין שלו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:3:2.english: His fire is due to his property - That is to say, it has the liability of his property, and not that the fire must be his; for even if he lit [a fire] with someone else's fire, he is liable, as we find in the chapter [entitled] HaKones (later, Bava Kamma 56a) regarding one who bends his fellow's standing grain in front of a fire and it reaches [it] by a normal wind, and regarding a spark that flies out from under the hammer, even though he presumably abandons it. And furthermore, [if the fire had to be his,] there would be no one who would be liable for a fire — for he would [simply] abandon the coals and burn his fellow's stack of grain! And [this is] not like Rashi, who explained that the difference between them is where he lit [a fire] with a coal that is not his.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:4:1.hebrew: רבי יוחנן מ"ט לא אמר כר"ל - אע"ג דדריש טעמא דר' יוחנן מקראי, הוה ליה לאוקמי קרא לדרשה אחריתי, דסברא כריש לקיש. א"נ, קס"ד השתא דמאן דאית ליה משום חציו לית ליה משום ממונו, וקבעי: היכא דכלו לו חציו, אמאי לא מחייב משום ממונו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:4:1.english: "Rabbi Yochanan — what is the reason he did not state [his opinion] in accordance with Reish Lakish?" - Even though Rabbi Yochanan's reasoning is derived from verses, he could have established the verse for another exposition, since logical reasoning accords with Reish Lakish. Alternatively, [the Gemara] currently assumes that one who holds [liability for fire is] on account of "his arrows" does not hold [it is] on account of "his property," and it is asking: where his arrows have ceased, why is he not liable on account of his property?

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:4:2.hebrew: ממונו אית ביה ממשא - אע"ג דבור לית ביה ממשא, שחייבה תורה להבלו ולא לחבטו, מ"מ ממונו כעין חציו שדרכו לילך ולהזיק — אית ביה ממשות. א"נ, בור נמי חשיב אית ביה ממשא, דע"י כריית הבור משתנה ממשות של קרקע ונעשה חלל, אבל מקום הילוך שלהבת אינו משתנה ממשותו אלא שנעשה דולק ושורף. וא"ת: ממונו נמי לית ביה ממשא, כגון צרורות ברוח שבכנפיהם בריש פירקין, דאיכא לסומכוס נ"ש? וי"ל: דמ"מ גוף הממון שפשע בו אית ביה ממשא, שיש לו לשמור ממונו שלא יזיק לא ברוח ולא בשום דבר, ואין שום ממון שלא יהא בו ממשא במה שפשע. אבל יש חץ שאין בו ממשות, כגון שיבר כלי ברוח פיו, ויש אש שאין בו ממשות, כגון שלהבת בלא גחלת, כדאמרינן בסוף ביצה (דף לט.); הילכך דמו להדדי, שאין בשניהם ממשות בהמזיק שפשע בו, רק בגוף האדם:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:4:2.english: "His property has substance" - Even though a pit has no substance — for the Torah obligated [one] for its noxious air and not for its impact — nevertheless, [the category of] "his property" that is like his arrows, which tends to go and cause damage, has substance. Alternatively, a pit is also considered to have substance, for through digging the pit the substance of the ground is altered and a cavity is formed, whereas the place where a flame passes does not have its substance altered, [but] rather becomes ignited and burning. And if you ask: [there is a case of] "his property" that also has no substance, such as pebbles [propelled] by the wind from their wings [mentioned] at the beginning of our chapter, where according to Symmachus there is [liability for] full damages? One can answer: that nevertheless the physical property itself regarding which he was negligent has substance, for he must guard his property so that it does not cause damage neither through wind nor through anything else, and there is no [case of] "property" that lacks substance in that regarding which he was negligent. However, there is [a case of] an "arrow" [i.e., direct force] that has no substance, such as [one who] broke a vessel with the breath of his mouth, and there is fire that has no substance, such as a flame without a coal, as we say at the end of Beitzah (39a); therefore they are comparable to one another, since in both of them there is no substance in the damaging agent regarding which he was negligent, only in the person's body [that generated it].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:6:1.hebrew: לאו ממונו דבעל כלב הוא - דהוא לא הדליקו, ועל אש של כלבו לא חייבתו תורה. ואע"ג דלגבי בור אצטריך מיעוט: "איש בור ולא שור בור", כדאמרינן בשור שנגח את הפרה (לקמן בבא קמא דף מח. ושם): תרי "איש" כתיב; מ"מ פשוט ליה לגמרא משום [איזה] דרשא דפטור על אש בהמתו, דג' אבות נאמרו בשור ולא יותר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:6:1.english: "[This fire] is not the property of the owner of the dog" - For he did not kindle it, and the Torah did not obligate him for his dog's fire. And even though regarding a pit an exclusion was needed — "a man [who digs] a pit, and not an ox [that digs] a pit," as we say in [the chapter] HaShor SheNagach Et HaParah (below, Bava Kamma 48a, and there): "man" is written twice — nevertheless, it is obvious to the Gemara, based on [some] exposition, that one is exempt for the fire of his animal, for [only] three primary categories [of damage] were stated regarding an ox and no more.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:7:1.hebrew: דאדייה אדויי - הו"מ לאוקמי באנח אנוחי ע"י שינוי, כדאמרינן בריש פירקין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:7:1.english: "Where it threw it" - [The Gemara] could have established [the Mishnah as a case] where it placed [the coal] down in an unusual manner, as we say at the beginning of our chapter.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:7:2.hebrew: ורבי יוחנן - בדאנחה אנוחי; לא מצי למימר באדייה אדויי ועל כל הגדיש ח"נ, דאי כח כחו לאו ככחו דמי, הוי על כל שאר הגדיש פטור:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:7:2.english: And Rabbi Yochanan - [explains it] as [a case where the dog] placed it down; he could not say [that it was a case of] throwing [it] and [that] for the entire stack [the owner pays] half-damage, for if his secondary force is not considered like his direct force, he would be exempt for all the rest of the stack:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:8:1.hebrew: ועל הגדיש ח"נ - ואע"ג דלגבי שולח בעירה לא מחייב עד דמסר לו שלהבת לר"ל, ולר' יוחנן עד דמסר לו גווזא — פעמים שיש גחלת הרבה בחררה, דהויא כמו מסר לו גווזא לר"י ושלהבת לר"ל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 22a:8:1.english: And for the stack [of grain], half-damages - And even though with respect to one who sends out a fire [with an incompetent person], he is not liable unless he hands over a flame to him according to Reish Lakish, and according to Rabbi Yoḥanan unless he hands over kindling to him — sometimes there is a large [amount of] coal on the cake, which is like handing over kindling according to Rabbi Yoḥanan and a flame according to Reish Lakish.
